metadata.name: Settings Panel
metadata.description: A settings panel for chat apps: tabs for general, notifications and data, theme with system, light and dark, message density, send with Enter and other switches, each with a short hint.
metadata.author: aadixc0de

A demo taller than its frame gets scrollbars, which * render white on dark pages. FitFrame fills the frame exactly instead. * * - "scale": the content shrinks until it fits, centered. For visuals such as orbs. * - "crop": the content stays at full size from the top and fades out at the bottom. For text * that streams in, where a changing scale would make the page breathe. * * `minWidth` lays out a wide demo (a table, a two column panel) at that width and scales it down * to the frame, instead of letting it collapse to a narrow layout. The frame centers it, so it * shrinks evenly on both sides. * * Anything marked `data-fit-hide` (state buttons, the chatcn.dev line) drops out in frames * shorter than `hideBelow`, so a profile card shows the visual alone. */ function FitFrame({ children, mode = "scale", hideBelow = 360, minWidth, }: { children: React.ReactNode mode?: "scale" | "crop" hideBelow?: number minWidth?: string }) { const content = React.useRef(null) const [cropped, setCropped] = React.useState(false) React.useLayoutEffect(() => { const el = content.current if (!el) return const measure = () => { const vw = window.innerWidth const vh = window.innerHeight el.toggleAttribute("data-fit-small", vh < hideBelow) // Layout sizes ignore the transform, so measuring never feeds back. const w = Math.max(el.offsetWidth, el.scrollWidth) const h = Math.max(el.offsetHeight, el.scrollHeight) const scale = mode === "scale" ? Math.min(1, vw / w, vh / h) : 1 el.style.transform = scale < 1 ? `scale(${scale})` : "" setCropped(mode === "crop" && h > vh + 1) } measure() const observer = new ResizeObserver(measure) observer.observe(el) // Content that changes inside a fixed width box (a headline that cycles words) never resizes // the box itself, so changes below it measure again on the next frame. let frame = 0 const mutations = new MutationObserver(() => { cancelAnimationFrame(frame) frame = requestAnimationFrame(measure) }) mutations.observe(el, { subtree: true, childList: true, characterData: true }) window.addEventListener("resize", measure) return () => { observer.disconnect() mutations.disconnect() cancelAnimationFrame(frame) window.removeEventListener("resize", measure) } }, [mode, hideBelow]) const fade = "linear-gradient(to bottom, #000 calc(100% - 40px), transparent)" return (
